pdfHello: Thank you for teaching our class today.
pdfIntro: Everything in this pack is review, so there is nothing new to teach. Each block has one worksheet for everyone and a short script on the next pages. The blocks do not fill the whole day: between them, follow our schedule (recess, lunch, specials) and use the list "When there is time between blocks" before the block scripts. The class information sheets at the back tell you how our day runs.
pdfBefore1: Read the class information sheets at the back of this pack. They say where the pencils, crayons, and paper are kept; several worksheets need crayons or colored pencils.
pdfBefore2: Find the copied worksheets and put them in stacks in the order of the list below. Each block has a stack for everyone; many blocks also have a few copies of an easier page and a stack for early finishers. If the copies have not been made, ask the office for help before the children arrive.
pdfBefore3: Write today's schedule on the board, so that the children can see what comes next.
pdfBefore4: Put one copy of the first worksheet on each desk.
pdfBefore5: Look through each worksheet and do its first item yourself, so that you can show it to the class. This pack has no answer key.
pdfAny1: Read the directions at the top of each worksheet aloud before the children start.
pdfAny2: A child who finishes early gets the page for early finishers, if the block has one. After that the child may read a book or draw on the back of the page. If most of the class is done before the block ends, collect the pages and go to the list "When there is time between blocks."
pdfAny3: Collect every worksheet at the end of its block and leave the stacks on the teacher's desk.
pdfAny4: Young children need to move. After every block, have the class stand and stretch for a minute before you hand out the next page.
pdfAny4_23: Children this age still need to move. After every block, have the class stand and stretch for a minute before you hand out the next page.
pdfHandOutText: {title}: the page for everyone. Give the easier page to the children listed on the class information sheets, and to any child who cannot get started after your help. Keep the page for early finishers ready.
pdfHandOutTextEasy: {title}: the page for everyone. Give the easier page to the children listed on the class information sheets, and to any child who cannot get started after your help.
pdfHandOutTextHard: {title}: the page for everyone. Keep the page for early finishers ready.
pdfMorningSay: "Good morning. My name is ___. Your teacher is out today, so I am your teacher for the day. Your first job is on your desk."
pdfMorningDo: While the children work, take attendance and lunch count.
pdfBell: Stop at least ten minutes before dismissal. Collect the pages, have the children clean up around their desks and pack their backpacks, and follow the dismissal list on the class information sheets. Make sure every child leaves the way the list says. If you are not sure how a child goes home or who may pick the child up, call the office; do not guess.
pdfFillTitle: When there is time between blocks
pdfFill1: Read a picture book aloud. The class information sheets say where the read-aloud books are. Stop two or three times and ask what might happen next.
pdfFill1_23: Read aloud from the chapter book the class is reading, or from a picture book. The class information sheets say where the read-aloud books are. Stop two or three times and ask what might happen next.
pdfFill2: Play a movement game the children know, such as Simon Says (nobody is out; everyone keeps playing), or count to 20 together with a clap, a stomp, or a jump on every number.
pdfFill2_23: Play a movement game the children know, such as Simon Says (nobody is out; everyone keeps playing), or count by fives or tens around the room: each child says the next number, the class helps anyone who is not sure, and the class starts over after 100.
pdfFill3: Let the children read or look at books on their own, at their seats or in the place the class uses for reading.
pdfFill4: Give each child a blank sheet of paper to draw something from the day. Children who can write add a word or a sentence about it.
pdfFill4_23: Give each child a blank sheet of paper to write three sentences about the day and to draw a picture that goes with them.
pdfFill5: Play I Spy: "I spy something that begins with the sound mmm," or "I spy something shaped like a circle." The child who guesses it gives the next clue.
pdfFill5_23: Play Twenty Questions: think of an animal or of something in the room, and let the children ask questions that you can answer with yes or no until someone guesses it. The child who guesses it thinks of the next one.
pdfReportLead: Please fill this in at the end of the day and leave it on the desk.

pdfReportHelp: Children who needed extra help, and with what
pdfReportGood: Children who were a great help today

pdfClassLead: The classroom teacher fills in these pages once and keeps a copy with the pack.
pdfClassList: Class list and seating chart (attach a copy)
pdfClassAttendance: Attendance and lunch count: how to take them and where to send them
pdfClassSchedule: Our day: times of arrival, snack, recess, lunch, specials, and dismissal, and where the class goes for each
pdfClassRoutines: Routines: attention signal, restroom, drinks, lining up; where pencils, crayons, paper, counters, and name tags are kept
pdfClassBehavior: Behavior: our class rules, how I reward good choices, what to do when a child does not follow directions
pdfClassEasier: Children who get the easier page: in reading and writing, in math
pdfClassPullouts: Children who leave the room: who, when, and where they go (speech, reading support, English learners, special education)
pdfClassExtra: If there is extra time: a book to read aloud and where it is, a song or game the class knows, where the children read on their own
pdfClassHelpers: Who can help: the teacher next door (name and room), the office (phone extension), children who know the routines
pdfClassNeeds: Children with allergies, medication, a behavior plan, or other needs (see the office or the nurse for details)
pdfClassDismissal: Dismissal: how each child goes home. List the bus riders with bus numbers, the car riders, the walkers, and the children in after-school care
pdfClassPickup: Who may pick up each child, and what to do when someone else comes for a child
pdfClassEmergency: Emergency procedures: fire drill, lockdown, and severe weather; where the plan and the class list are kept; our way out of the building
hubMetaTitle: Emergency Sub Plans by Grade: No-Prep Days of Review
hubMetaDescription: Emergency sub plans by grade: days of review for the start, middle, and end of the year, each with a worksheet for every block and a script for the guest teacher.
hubEyebrow: For the day you are out
hubLead: A sub plan here is one school day of review for one grade, ready to print. Every block of the day has a worksheet for the whole class and a short script that tells the guest teacher what to say, how to start, and what to do when a child is stuck. The blocks are seat work that fits around recess, lunch, and specials; the guest teacher pages list what to do in between. Each grade has plans for the start, the middle, and the end of the year, with two different days for each, so the work should be something your class has already learned.
